title: Program wire — cross-layer reference (§9.2)
description: A composition surface naming a program by identifier, optionally content-addressed. The opaqueness this family exists for is enforced by `additionalProperties: false` over a declaration that states the ONLY members there are — so an inline body, an evaluation hint or an interpretation tag is refused as undeclared, including the ones nobody has thought of yet. A blocklist could only ever cover the ones somebody had.

hash.description: The content address of the demand projection published under `ref` (§9.2). OPTIONAL: absent means unpinned, which is the posture every reference took before this member existed, and is a different fact from 'any document will do'. The pattern is the whole of what a schema can say here — that the recomputed address must EQUAL this value is §9.2 obligation 2, which needs the addressed document and so belongs to the text.

ref.description: The identifier under which the host holds the program. A bounded reference and nothing else — never the program.

slot.description: The slot identity. It is a (namespace, kind) PAIR rendered here joined with `/`; a host whose registry joins the same pair differently derives both renderings from the pair rather than storing either string twice (§9.2).
